title: Sensex jumps 1,600 points at open as oil slides after US midterms
dek: Brent fell to about $93.50 a barrel as traders bet on lower risk of escalation with Iran; the Nifty opened 1.7% higher.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Indian shares opened sharply higher on Thursday as oil prices tumbled after the US midterm elections, with the Sensex jumping more than 1,600 points at the start of trade.

The BSE Sensex opened at 78,910.94, up 1,609.54 points, or about 2%, from Wednesday's close of 77,301.40, and touched 78,922.44 in early deals, Upstox and Outlook Money reported. The NSE Nifty 50 opened 417.45 points, or 1.74%, higher at 24,378.05. Forty-two of the 50 Nifty stocks were in the green in early trade, led by Shriram Finance, IndiGo and Bajaj Finance; Apollo Hospitals and ONGC were the biggest fallers. The gains extend the indices' winning run to a sixth session.

Brent crude fell to an intraday low of $93.50 a barrel on Thursday morning, according to Upstox, from a high of $104.96 on Wednesday. Oil had already dropped below $100 on Wednesday for the first time since September. Traders read the Democrats' win in both houses of the US Congress as lowering the risk of further US escalation against Iran and of new disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. India imports most of its crude oil, so lower prices ease pressure on inflation and the rupee.

Foreign investors were net buyers for a third straight session on Wednesday, according to provisional exchange data reported by Outlook Money. These are opening figures; the market closes at 3.30 pm IST.
